is_record/1: Pinned is_record_1 tests the native-record header only. The managed predicate is exactly NativeRecordTerm. Tuple records, all other ordinary term families and real interior HAMT nodes return false; module, name, field count/defaults and exportedness do not affect the result.
is_record/2: Validate the second argument as an atom before inspecting the first. A nonempty tuple matches its first element; a native record matches its name only, ignoring its module, fields and exportedness. Everything else returns false. Invalid tags preserve badarg, all original arguments and the complete native/caller stack. Atom equality is exact name equality, including empty and Unicode names.
is_record/3: Validate the second argument as an atom first. An atom third argument selects native-record identity, comparing both module and name via the pinned erl_is_native_record relation. A native-small integer selects tuple arity and first-element tag; other third types and out-of-small-range integers raise badarg. On the admitted64-bit VM, the exact signed range is[-2^59,2^59-1]. Empty tuples have no tag and return false, including size0; negative/mismatching sizes also return false. Fields, defaults and exportedness never affect native identity.
Dispatch: Every page has actual dynamic apply instructions and immutable reviewed worker/support ownership. Direct calls and legal literal guards compare original optimizer-selected paths as well. Variable record tags and invalid tag/size expressions cannot be used as source guards in pinned OTP; their error partitions remain ordinary BIF calls, not invented guard semantics. The existing bif3 dispatch is extended only from erlang:is_integer/3 to include erlang:is_record/3.
